newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to Slovnaft push Slovak bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Gains to Slovnaft push Slovak bourse higher.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with strong gains in oil refiner Slovnaft pushing the SAX index 1.07 points higher to 190.9.
Slovnaft, the most-heavily capitalised issue on the BSE floor, gained 50 crowns to close at 850. Brokers said the gains could extend to around 900 crowns.
Despite low volumes on the BSE main floor -- only 5,322 shares traded on Monday -- strong foreign demand should help the bourse maintain the uptrend, dealers said.

"We think that the current strong demand from foreign investors should keep the market running up for some time, and that the SAX can even break the 200-point level in foreseeable future," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
He said investors were interested mainly in the most liquid and lucrative Slovak blue chips, such as steel maker VSZ, Slovnaft or drug maker Slovakofarma.
VSZ led today's trading on the BSE floor with 4,779 stocks changing hands, but the stock closed unchanged at 670 crowns.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta finished five crowns lower at 1,695.
Brokers said that despite the uncertanity over the firm's future which has brought cautious approach by investors, Nafta's current price appeared to reflect the stock's real value.
Overall volume rose to 763,984 shares, mainly direct trades, from 528,114 changing hands on Friday. Turnover increased to 837.56 million crowns, from 480.69 million.
